decision: Should the close block's multi-step row hand a line that runs with no keystroke (`cc-do --run`), or keep bare `cc-do` and its one Enter as the consent step?
recommendation: Drop the Enter: the close row should hand `cc-do --run` as a flag at the end of the line, never as an environment-variable prefix, and the rule's "confirms once" wording should change to match; but do not adopt this option's permission-harvest hand-off, and hand the operator the line that worked for him on 2026-10-01 instead.
why: The operator's own ruling settles this. On 2026-09-24 he asked for handed commands that need no user interaction "in a regular Terminal" (I read it at transcript ac782148…jsonl line 225), and that became CLAUDE.global.md:1059-1068 in commit 59c228e90. The only exceptions it allows are prompts the OS or a vendor demands. No memory note or operator message makes cc-do's Enter an exception, so keeping the Enter would mean overturning a ruling that is 10 days old.

The Enter is weak consent and is almost never answered. The prompt is `[Y/n]` and an empty answer means yes (bin/cc-do:542-547). Both bare `!cc-do` board runs on record ended in NOTHING RAN, and no terminal run was ever observed (transcript counts from both evidence axes). When the board refuses, cc-do already tells the operator to paste `cc-do --run` (bin/cc-do:535-540), and a single runnable item already runs with no prompt (bin/cc-do:467-499). So this change picks which existing line gets handed; cc-do's code does not change.

The option's permission-harvest half fails as written. Commands run with `!` inherit CLAUDECODE: on 2026-10-02 the operator's `!agent-secrets add` printed the inside-an-agent-session note, and that check tests CLAUDECODE first (~/.agent-secrets/lib/common.sh:158-160). So `CC_DO_ASSUME_YES=1 cc-do b13ef5862c83` would hit the tool's exit-4 refusal (bin/cc-permission-harvest:2070-2080). Of the 13 rows cc-do has ever closed, none is a harvest row (measured with jq on backlog.jsonl). The route that worked was the operator's own `!env -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT CONFIRM=1 ~/.claude/bin/cc-permission-harvest --bang --apply` on 2026-10-01 (9aa483e9…jsonl record 835). The validate-bash deny arm blocks agents from running that line (hooks/validate-bash.sh:1543), but it cannot see through `cc-do <id>`.

The real remaining risk is consent without a named target. `cc-do --run` runs whatever is queued when the operator pastes it (bin/cc-do:504,525). On 2026-09-04 the board held two harmful activations, but an Enter that defaults to yes would not have stopped them either. That gap was closed by `.superseded` markers (hooks/activation-marker.sh:8-19). The 2 items runnable today, 44 and 49, are reversible, and the row names them because there are 3 or fewer (hooks/operator-readout.sh:1348). A follow-up should make `--run` refuse when the stems it finds differ from the ones shown.
what_would_change_it:
Things that would lower this:
- The operator says he wants the Enter kept as a review step. His word outranks the inference from 2026-09-24.
- Evidence that he regularly runs bare `cc-do` in a real terminal.
- An activation that writes settings, allowlists or permissions lands on the runnable path. Target binding (refusing when the runnable stems differ from those shown) would then be required before the change, not after it.
- Proof that `!` does not inherit CLAUDECODE. The option's harvest hand-off would then work, though it would still hand over an allowlist write as a bare id.

The per-row `cc-do <id>` typed yes is outside this decision. It caused 19 of the 22 NOTHING RAN events (the skeptic's transcript count), and neither option fixes it, so it needs its own decision.

I made no edits. My checks were read-only: sed/rg/jq over the repo, transcripts and backlog.jsonl, plus `cc-backlog list --blocked --json`.
conviction_moved:
It moved from 65% to 80%.

**Upward:**
- I read the operator's 2026-09-24 message myself. It rules out interaction in a regular Terminal too, not only under `!`, which removes keep-enter's "run it in a terminal tab" fallback.
- No operator ruling sanctions the Enter.
- The prompt defaults to yes.
- cc-do already prints `cc-do --run` as the line to paste.

**What kept it below 85:**
- The skeptic is right that the option as worded breaks for permission-harvest. I confirmed that `!` carries CLAUDECODE, which makes the harvest tool refuse.
- `--run` names no target, so the line authorises whatever is queued at paste time.

Both are fixable inside drop-enter, so neither is a reason to keep the Enter. That is why I rate drop-enter, adjusted, well above the skeptic's 35% for the option as worded.

decision: Which effort setting should research-program certification reviewers on the Anthropic lane be pinned to?
recommendation: Pin Opus 5.5 reviewers at xhigh, not high, and keep the Fable 5.1 reviewers in the frontier slots at high: store a separate effort for each vendor next to reviewer_pins in frame.json, pass it as --effort, record it on each panel next to pinned_model, and have check-round void any panel that ran at a different effort.
why: The evidence behind the lean toward high is misquoted and has been replaced. The single-sample sweep scored Opus 5.5 at medium 8, high 8 and xhigh 10, and its p=0.38 compares Opus 5.5 at xhigh with Opus 5 at max, not two effort levels (opus55-effort-sweep-2026-09-22/README.md:73, :110). The repo's 3-sample, two-panel follow-up has xhigh beating high on mean recall, 12.7 v 9.3, with 3 items v 0 and 12 cells v 2 (cells p=0.013) under both panels (review-judge-followup-2026-09-22/README.md:96-97, :127, :132). The item-level p is still 0.25, so this is a consistent direction, not a significant result.

Your own routing rule already sets this level. CLAUDE.global.md:347 says code review and long-horizon knowledge work run at xhigh, and model-config.yaml:1358-1367 says 'review runs at xhigh, not the opus55_default high'. The reviewer brief is an open-ended read of a whole plan bundle across 11 lenses, not a bounded check, which the config puts at high (opus55-utilization README:58-59).

The best argument for high is matching the calibration, and it is weaker than it looks. The calibration ran every Anthropic slot as Opus 5.5 at high (research-calibration/workflows/review.workflow.js:27; REPORT.md:69-71). But the live program already differs from that setup in three ways: Fable fills the frontier slots (preflight.json), Opus ran at medium, and the OpenAI reviewers ran at xhigh, inherited from ~/.codex/config.toml:2. The false-alarm share also re-measures itself from the program's own verifier once data exists (estimate.py:366-376). If xhigh finds more holes, the calibrated recall terms simply become conservative.

Cost is small, and you have ruled that spends this size need no ask. My estimate is about +0.04 to +0.28 weekly percentage points per round for xhigh over high. I got it by scaling the measured 0.05 pp per read (research-calibration/REPORT.md:168-171) by the measured token ratios: 1.08x with tools (synth-reprobe README:203-204) and 2.4x without tools (followup README:218). That falls well under the 2-4 pp in feedback-small-quota-spend-needs-no-ask.md. The one comparison of these two levels with tools also favoured xhigh on bad citations (5.2% v 11.6%) and wrong claims (18 v 24) (synth-reprobe README:200-204).
what_would_change_it:
The decision would flip back to high, or to a deliberate recalibration first, if a repeated measurement on certification-style plan review showed Opus 5.5 at xhigh raising more false material calls per read than at high. The method's binding problem is false alarms, at 1.13 per read (research-calibration/REPORT.md:88), and no sweep has scored false alarms by effort. It would also change if you rule that the frozen method v1.1 (SKILL.md:8-9) treats the calibrated detector, Opus at high, as part of the method. Separately from this decision, I found three fixes the packet does not mention:
- The packet's premise is wrong. No Sonnet 5.5 reviewer slot exists. The frontier lane is Fable 5.1, which already runs at high, confirmed from the effort field in the fc1/fc2 transcripts, and it should be pinned at high, not xhigh (model-config.yaml:1299-1305).
- The OpenAI lane is also unpinned. It should get an explicit -c model_reasoning_effort setting instead of inheriting it from ~/.codex/config.toml.
- The code that builds the reviewer command (argv_for) does not know whether it is launching a reviewer, rater or verifier, so a pin would also set the effort of Anthropic verifiers. Verifiers are bounded checks, which the config puts at high.
conviction_moved: The prior was 60% for high. It is now 80% for xhigh on Opus 5.5 reviewers, a reversal. Four things I checked myself moved it. First, the packet's receipt misquotes the single-sample sweep: high scored 8, not 9, and p=0.38 is not an effort comparison. Second, the 3-sample follow-up, which the packet did not cite, shows xhigh over high under both judge panels. Third, your global rule and the model config already put code review at xhigh. Fourth, the case for matching the calibration is weakened because the live rounds already depart from the calibrated setup: Opus at medium, Fable at high, OpenAI at xhigh. Three things keep it below 90, so this still goes to you: the item-level p is 0.25, effort has never been tested against false alarms, and the calibrated detector was Opus at high. The two evidence axes and the skeptic were all read-only, and so was I; nothing was edited and no model was run.

decision: Should we spend about 100 model runs now re-testing the live slim instructions on 10 new tasks, wait and run it with the next slim edit, or never re-test?
recommendation: Don't spend the runs yet: this week, at no quota cost, write and freeze the 10 new tasks (including tasks on slim's known weak spots) and repair the test harness for today's file layout, then run them as the test for the next slim edit, which is already queued.
why: As proposed, the run cannot pass. I checked this with agg.py's own newcombe() function: even a perfect 50-out-of-50 tie in each arm gives a success lower bound of -7.1 points, outside the -5 point margin, so the only possible results are FAIL or inconclusive (agg.py:8-18).

The harness breaks on today's layout. build-arms.sh:12-17 refuses to run because the variant status reads STALE. It also copies the 27,675-byte slim file as the 'full' arm, and it copies rules/agent-operating-lessons.md, which no longer exists (checked with ls ~/.claude/rules/). Its exclude list at run.sh:62-64 does not cover the 30,994-byte close-rules file, so that file would leak into both arms.

Data already in hand gives a bigger held-out-style reading for free. I re-split the pooled per-task table (report.md:131-151) and recomputed with agg.py: on the 13 tasks no editing round used, slim scored 183/195 against full's 191/195, which is -4.1 points (CI -8.6 to -0.1). So the worry that the pass was scored on the same tasks used to tune slim is real. The gap is probably overstated, though: the post-hoc split favours this pattern by regression to the mean, and dropping the judge-variance task gives -2.8 points (CI -7.2 to +1.3). The losses sit on the 'answer the question asked' and 'mark plan done' tasks, which the proposed task mix does not target.

The next slim edit is effectively certain. Open decision 5cee611ac837 rewrites the zero-keystroke and cc-do hand-over lines (CLAUDE.rules.slim.10-session-close.md:207-211) whichever way the operator rules, so a run now would test text that is about to change. Cost is not the reason to wait: about 3-7 weekly points in total is inside the operator's no-ask band, and next2 sits at 2% weekly until its 10-10 reset (account-utilization.jsonl, 17:29Z).
what_would_change_it: Run sooner if any of these happens. (1) A live false 'good to close', a re-issued refused push or a chained hand-over shows up while slim alone is loaded. (2) The model or Claude Code version changes from the one the gate ran on. (3) The tasks and harness are ready but no slim edit is in sight, and next2 is still on course to waste quota: then run the new tasks against the current slim right away, which costs nearly nothing. (4) The operator says they want the train-score question settled now anyway. Two things would lower my conviction. One is the operator ruling that the full text should be redeployable. Today it is 113,341 chars, against the enforced 40k-per-file budget. The other is the T14/T18 shortfall failing to reproduce in a cheap targeted probe. Either would make the held-out run matter less.
conviction_moved: Starting point: the audit recommended running this (REPORT.md section 3) and gave no number, asking for approval only because of cost. I moved away from running now for four reasons, each checked myself: (1) the design cannot return a pass; (2) the harness breaks on the current two-file layout; (3) the data already in hand reads the held-out question more precisely than 50 runs per arm would; (4) the open cc-do decision will edit the hand-over rules either way. I moved away from never because the re-split confirms the train-score worry is real, and because the operator's own rulings remove cost as an objection: small spends need no ask, and unused quota does not roll over. I capped conviction at 70 for two reasons. Those same rulings, plus the memory lesson that a deferral nothing triggers becomes 'never', argue for running something this week. And the -4.1 point reading is post-hoc and probably inflated by regression to the mean. I checked the evidence files and made no changes.
